about: Sourced life stories for the kings of Israel (Jeroboam I to Hoshea) and the kings and queen of Judah (Rehoboam to Zedekiah). Written from Scripture and the reviewed dossiers Research/People/rulers-israel.md and Research/People/rulers-judah.md.

jeroboam-1ki-11-26.short: Jeroboam son of Nebat, once Solomon's servant, became the first king of the ten northern tribes and set up golden calves at Beth-el and Dan.

paragraphs.text: Jeroboam was the son of Nebat, an Ephrathite of Zereda, and his mother was Zeruah, a widow. He was “a mighty man of valour”, and Solomon, seeing that he was industrious, put him over all the labour of the house of Joseph.

When Jeroboam went out of Jerusalem, the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite met him alone in the field, tore a new garment into twelve pieces, and told him to take ten: the LORD would give him ten tribes. Ahijah promised him “a sure house, as I built for David”, if he would keep God's ways. Solomon sought to kill him, and he fled to Shishak king of Egypt until Solomon died.

After Solomon's death the people sent for Jeroboam, who was still in Egypt, and he and all the congregation of Israel asked Rehoboam to lighten their yoke. When Rehoboam refused, the northern tribes made Jeroboam king over all Israel; only Judah followed the house of David.

Jeroboam said in his heart that if the people went up to sacrifice in Jerusalem, the kingdom would return to the house of David. So he made two calves of gold and set one in Beth-el and the other in Dan, made priests who were not of the sons of Levi, and ordained a feast in the eighth month. A man of God from Judah cried against his altar at Beth-el; Jeroboam's hand dried up when he stretched it out against him, and was restored when the man prayed.

When his son Abijah fell sick, he sent his wife in disguise to Ahijah, who foretold the end of Jeroboam's house, and the child died as she came to the threshold. Kings says “Jeroboam returned not from his evil way”. There was war between him and Rehoboam all their days; after twenty-two years “he slept with his fathers”, and Nadab his son reigned. Chronicles adds that he did not recover strength in the days of Abijah king of Judah, “and the LORD struck him, and he died”.

nadab-1ki-14-20.short: Jeroboam's son Nadab reigned two years and was killed by Baasha at the siege of Gibbethon; with him the whole house of Jeroboam was destroyed.

paragraphs.text: Nadab was the son of Jeroboam, and reigned in his place when his father died. He began to reign over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned two years. Kings says “he did evil in the sight of the LORD, and walked in the way of his father”.

While Nadab and all Israel were besieging Gibbethon, a town of the Philistines, Baasha son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, conspired against him and killed him there, in the third year of Asa, and reigned in his place. Baasha then struck down all the house of Jeroboam, as Ahijah the Shilonite had foretold. Scripture tells nothing more of Nadab's life.

baasha-1ki-15-16.short: Baasha of the house of Issachar killed King Nadab, destroyed Jeroboam's house, and reigned twenty-four years in Tirzah, at war with Asa of Judah.

paragraphs.text: Baasha was the son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar. He conspired against Nadab son of Jeroboam while Israel was besieging Gibbethon, killed him there in the third year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned in his place. As soon as he reigned he struck down all the house of Jeroboam, leaving none that breathed.

He reigned twenty-four years in Tirzah, and “there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days”. He built Ramah so that none could go out or come in to Asa, until Asa paid Ben-hadad king of Syria to break his league with Baasha; Ben-hadad struck cities of Israel, and Baasha left off building Ramah. Chronicles dates his coming against Judah to the thirty-sixth year of Asa's reign.

Kings says “he did evil in the sight of the LORD, and walked in the way of Jeroboam”. Jehu son of Hanani brought him the word of the LORD: “I exalted thee out of the dust”, but because he had walked in the way of Jeroboam, his house would be like Jeroboam's. Baasha slept with his fathers and was buried in Tirzah, and Elah his son reigned in his place.

elah-1ki-16-6.short: Baasha's son Elah reigned two years in Tirzah and was killed by Zimri, one of his chariot captains, while drinking in his steward's house.

paragraphs.text: Elah was the son of Baasha and reigned in his place. He began to reign over Israel in Tirzah in the twenty-sixth year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned two years. Scripture tells only how his reign ended.

Elah was in Tirzah, “drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza steward of his house”, when his servant Zimri, captain of half his chariots, went in and killed him, in Asa's twenty-seventh year, and reigned in his place. Zimri then killed all the house of Baasha, as Jehu the prophet had spoken. Kings joins Elah to his father's sins, by which they provoked the LORD “with their vanities”.

zimri-1ki-16-9.short: Zimri, captain of half King Elah's chariots, killed his master and reigned seven days in Tirzah before dying in the burning palace.

paragraphs.text: Zimri was a servant of King Elah, “captain of half his chariots”; Scripture names no father for him. He conspired against Elah, killed him in Tirzah, and reigned in his place, and as soon as he sat on the throne he killed all the house of Baasha.

He reigned seven days. The army encamped at Gibbethon heard that Zimri had killed the king, and made Omri, the captain of the host, king that day in the camp. Omri came up and besieged Tirzah, and when Zimri saw that the city was taken, he went into the palace, “burnt the king's house over him with fire, and died”. Later, Jezebel threw his name at Jehu: “Had Zimri peace, who slew his master?”

omri-1ki-16-16.short: Omri, captain of Israel's army, was made king in the camp at Gibbethon, overcame Zimri and Tibni, and built Samaria on a hill he bought.

paragraphs.text: Omri was “the captain of the host” of Israel. When the army besieging Gibbethon heard that Zimri had killed King Elah, all Israel made Omri king that day in the camp. He went up from Gibbethon and besieged Tirzah, and when the city was taken Zimri died in the burning palace.

The people of Israel were then divided: half followed Tibni the son of Ginath, and half followed Omri. Omri's side prevailed, “so Tibni died, and Omri reigned”. He began to reign in the thirty-first year of Asa king of Judah and reigned twelve years, six of them in Tirzah.

He bought the hill Samaria from Shemer for two talents of silver, built on it, and named the city Samaria after Shemer, the owner of the hill. Kings says Omri “wrought evil in the eyes of the LORD, and did worse than all that were before him”. He slept with his fathers, was buried in Samaria, and Ahab his son reigned in his place.

ahab-1ki-16-28.short: Omri's son Ahab reigned twenty-two years in Samaria, married Jezebel and served Baal, was confronted by Elijah, and died of an arrow at Ramoth-gilead.

paragraphs.text: Ahab was the son of Omri and reigned in his place. He began to reign in the thirty-eighth year of Asa king of Judah and reigned twenty-two years in Samaria. He married Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Zidonians, served Baal, and reared up an altar for Baal in the house of Baal that he built in Samaria. Kings says he “did evil in the sight of the LORD above all that were before him”.

Elijah the Tishbite told him there would be neither dew nor rain but by his word. Jezebel cut off the prophets of the LORD, and Obadiah, who was over Ahab's house, hid a hundred of them by fifty in a cave. On Mount Carmel fire fell on Elijah's offering, the people cried “The LORD, he is the God”, and afterwards there was a great rain.

Ben-hadad king of Syria besieged Samaria and was beaten, and the next year was beaten again at Aphek. Ahab spared him and made a covenant with him, and a prophet told the king: “thy life shall go for his life, and thy people for his people”.

Naboth the Jezreelite would not sell Ahab his vineyard, so Jezebel wrote letters in Ahab's name, and Naboth was stoned. When Ahab went down to take the vineyard, Elijah met him there with the LORD's judgement; Ahab rent his clothes and fasted, and the LORD said he would bring the evil not in his days but “in his son's days”. Kings says there was none like Ahab, “whom Jezebel his wife stirred up”.

With Jehoshaphat king of Judah he went up to take Ramoth-gilead, though Micaiah son of Imlah foretold Israel scattered “as sheep that have not a shepherd”. Ahab disguised himself, but a man drew a bow “at a venture”, and the arrow struck him between the joints of the harness; he was held up in his chariot and died at evening. They buried him in Samaria, and the dogs licked up his blood at the pool of Samaria; Ahaziah his son reigned in his place.

ahaziah-1ki-22-40.short: Ahab's son Ahaziah reigned two years in Samaria; after a fall he sent to ask Baal-zebub of Ekron, and died as Elijah said, leaving no son.

paragraphs.text: Ahaziah was the son of Ahab and reigned in his place. He began to reign over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and reigned two years. Kings says he walked “in the way of his father, and in the way of his mother”, and served Baal. After Ahab's death Moab rebelled against Israel.

Kings says that he asked Jehoshaphat to let his servants go with Jehoshaphat's ships, “But Jehoshaphat would not”. Chronicles tells it otherwise: Jehoshaphat joined himself with Ahaziah to make ships at Ezion-geber, the prophet Eliezer spoke against it, and “the ships were broken”.

Ahaziah fell down through a lattice in his upper chamber in Samaria and sent messengers to ask Baal-zebub the god of Ekron whether he would recover. Elijah met them: “Is it not because there is not a God in Israel, that ye go to enquire of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron?” Two captains with their fifties, sent to bring Elijah, were consumed by fire from heaven; Elijah went down with the third and told the king to his face that he would die.
“So he died according to the word of the LORD which Elijah had spoken.” Because he had no son, Jehoram, another son of Ahab, reigned in his place.

joram-2ki-1-17.short: Ahab's son Joram reigned twelve years in Samaria, put away his father's image of Baal, and was shot by Jehu in the field of Naboth.

paragraphs.text: Jehoram, also called Joram, was a son of Ahab, and Jehu speaks to him of “thy mother Jezebel”. He reigned in place of his brother Ahaziah, who had no son, from the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and reigned twelve years in Samaria. Kings says he did evil in the sight of the LORD, “but not like his father, and like his mother: for he put away the image of Baal that his father had made”.

When Mesha king of Moab rebelled, Joram went out with Jehoshaphat king of Judah and the king of Edom. In the wilderness of Edom they had no water; Elisha said he would not have looked at Joram, “were it not that I regard the presence of Jehoshaphat”, and promised water. Moab was beaten back, and at Kir-haraseth Mesha offered his eldest son on the wall, and the kings returned to their own land.

With Ahaziah king of Judah he fought Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth-gilead, was wounded, and went back to Jezreel to be healed. Meanwhile a young prophet sent by Elisha anointed Jehu king over Israel. When Jehu came, Joram went out to meet him in the portion of Naboth the Jezreelite and asked, “Is it peace, Jehu?” As Joram turned to flee, Jehu's arrow went out at his heart, and Jehu told his captain to cast the body into Naboth's field, “according to the word of the LORD”.

jehu-1ki-19-16.short: Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi, anointed king at Ramoth-gilead, ended the house of Ahab and Baal worship in Israel, and reigned twenty-eight years.

paragraphs.text: Jehu was “the son of Jehoshaphat the son of Nimshi”. The LORD told Elijah to anoint him king over Israel. Elisha later sent one of the sons of the prophets to Ramoth-gilead, where Jehu sat among the captains of the host; the young man anointed him in an inner room and charged him to strike the house of Ahab. The captains spread their garments under him, blew with trumpets and said, “Jehu is king.”

He drove “furiously” to Jezreel and shot Joram king of Israel, and his men struck down Ahaziah king of Judah as he fled. Jezebel was thrown down from a window; when they went to bury her they found only her skull, feet and palms, and Jehu said this was the word Elijah had spoken, that dogs would eat her flesh. By letters to Samaria he had the seventy sons of Ahab killed, and he killed forty-two men who said they were brethren of Ahaziah king of Judah, at the shearing house.

He took Jehonadab the son of Rechab into his chariot: “Come with me, and see my zeal for the LORD.” Then he called a great sacrifice for Baal, had the worshippers of Baal killed in the house of Baal, and broke the house down. “Thus Jehu destroyed Baal out of Israel.”

The LORD told him “thou hast done well”, and promised that his sons would sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation. Yet he did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam, the golden calves in Beth-el and Dan, and “took no heed to walk in the law of the LORD God of Israel with all his heart”. In his days Hazael struck Israel east of the Jordan. He reigned twenty-eight years in Samaria, slept with his fathers, was buried in Samaria, and Jehoahaz his son reigned in his place.

jehoahaz-2ki-10-35.short: Jehu's son Jehoahaz reigned seventeen years in Samaria under the hand of Syria; he besought the LORD, who gave Israel a saviour.

paragraphs.text: Jehoahaz was the son of Jehu and reigned in his place. He began to reign over Israel in Samaria in the twenty-third year of Joash king of Judah, and reigned seventeen years. Kings says he “did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, and followed the sins of Jeroboam”.

The LORD delivered Israel into the hand of Hazael king of Syria and of Ben-hadad his son. “Jehoahaz besought the LORD, and the LORD hearkened unto him”, and gave Israel a saviour, so that they went out from under the hand of the Syrians. Even so, he was left only fifty horsemen, ten chariots and ten thousand footmen. He slept with his fathers, was buried in Samaria, and Joash his son reigned in his place.

joash-2ki-13-9.short: Jehoahaz's son Jehoash wept over the dying Elisha, beat Syria three times, defeated Amaziah of Judah, and reigned sixteen years in Samaria.

paragraphs.text: Jehoash, also called Joash, was the son of Jehoahaz and reigned in his place. He began to reign over Israel in Samaria in the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, and reigned sixteen years. Kings says he “did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD” and did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam.

When Elisha was sick of the sickness he died of, the king came down and wept over him: “O my father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof.” Elisha had him shoot an arrow eastward and then strike the ground; he struck three times and stopped, and Elisha said he would now beat Syria only three times. Three times Joash beat Ben-hadad son of Hazael, and he took back the cities that had been taken from his father Jehoahaz.

Amaziah king of Judah challenged him, and he answered with the parable of the thistle and the cedar in Lebanon. At Beth-shemesh Judah was beaten; Jehoash took Amaziah, broke down four hundred cubits of Jerusalem's wall, and carried the gold and silver of the house of the LORD and of the king's house, with hostages, to Samaria. Chronicles adds that soldiers of Israel whom Amaziah had hired and sent home fell on the cities of Judah. Jehoash slept with his fathers, was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel, and Jeroboam his son reigned in his place.

jeroboam-2ki-13-13.short: Jeroboam son of Joash reigned forty-one years in Samaria and restored Israel's borders, as Jonah had foretold; Amos and Hosea prophesied in his days.

paragraphs.text: Jeroboam was the son of Joash (Jehoash) king of Israel and reigned in his place. He began to reign in Samaria in the fifteenth year of Amaziah king of Judah, and reigned forty-one years. Kings says “he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD” and did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat.

He restored the coast of Israel “from the entering of Hamath unto the sea of the plain”, as the LORD had spoken by his servant Jonah the son of Amittai. Kings says the LORD saw that Israel's affliction was very bitter, and “saved them by the hand of Jeroboam the son of Joash”. It adds that the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel told how he recovered Damascus and Hamath for Israel.

Amos and Hosea both date their words to his days. Amaziah the priest of Beth-el sent to tell him that Amos had said, “Jeroboam shall die by the sword”; Kings says that Jeroboam “slept with his fathers, even with the kings of Israel”, and Zachariah his son reigned in his place. Chronicles names a Jeroboam king of Israel once, in a genealogy reckoned “in the days of Jotham king of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam king of Israel”.

zechariah-2ki-14-29.short: Jeroboam II's son Zachariah reigned six months in Samaria and was killed by Shallum, the last king of Jehu's line.

paragraphs.text: Zachariah was the son of Jeroboam son of Joash and reigned in his place. He reigned over Israel in Samaria six months, in the thirty-eighth year of Azariah king of Judah. Kings says “he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, as his fathers had done”.

Shallum the son of Jabesh conspired against him, “smote him before the people, and slew him”, and reigned in his place. Kings sees here the end of the LORD's word to Jehu: “Thy sons shall sit on the throne of Israel unto the fourth generation. And so it came to pass.” Scripture tells nothing more of him.

shallum-2ki-15-10.short: Shallum son of Jabesh killed King Zachariah and reigned one month in Samaria before Menahem killed him.

paragraphs.text: Shallum was the son of Jabesh. He conspired against Zachariah son of Jeroboam, “smote him before the people, and slew him, and reigned in his stead”, in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah.

He reigned “a full month in Samaria”. Then Menahem the son of Gadi came up from Tirzah to Samaria, struck Shallum and killed him, and reigned in his place. Kings gives Shallum no verdict; it says only that his conspiracy is written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

menahem-2ki-15-14.short: Menahem son of Gadi killed Shallum, reigned ten years in Samaria, and paid Pul king of Assyria a thousand talents of silver.

paragraphs.text: Menahem was the son of Gadi. He went up from Tirzah to Samaria, killed Shallum, and reigned in his place. He struck Tiphsah and its coasts “because they opened not to him”, and ripped up the women there who were with child.

He began to reign over Israel in the thirty-ninth year of Azariah king of Judah, and reigned ten years in Samaria. Kings says “he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD”. When Pul the king of Assyria came against the land, Menahem gave him a thousand talents of silver, taking fifty shekels from each of the mighty men of wealth, and Pul turned back. Menahem slept with his fathers, and Pekahiah his son reigned in his place.

pekahiah-2ki-15-22.short: Menahem's son Pekahiah reigned two years in Samaria and was killed in his palace by Pekah, one of his captains.

paragraphs.text: Pekahiah was the son of Menahem and reigned in his place. He began to reign over Israel in Samaria in the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah, and reigned two years. Kings says “he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD”.

Pekah the son of Remaliah, a captain of his, conspired against him and struck him in Samaria, “in the palace of the king's house, with Argob and Arieh, and with him fifty men of the Gileadites”, and reigned in his place. Kings records nothing else of Pekahiah's life.

pekah-2ki-15-25.short: Pekah son of Remaliah killed Pekahiah, reigned twenty years, warred on Judah with Rezin of Syria, lost Galilee and Gilead to Assyria, and was killed by Hoshea.

paragraphs.text: Pekah was the son of Remaliah and a captain of King Pekahiah. He conspired against the king and killed him in his palace in Samaria, “with him fifty men of the Gileadites”, and reigned in his place. He began to reign in the fifty-second year of Azariah king of Judah and reigned twenty years. Kings says “he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD”.

With Rezin king of Syria he came against Judah and besieged Ahaz in Jerusalem, “but could not overcome him”. Isaiah told Ahaz not to fear “the two tails of these smoking firebrands”, Rezin and the son of Remaliah. Chronicles adds that Pekah killed a hundred and twenty thousand in Judah in one day, and that Israel carried away two hundred thousand captives, whom they sent home at the word of the prophet Oded.

In his days Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria took Ijon, Abel-beth-maachah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, Galilee and all the land of Naphtali, and carried the people captive to Assyria. Then Hoshea the son of Elah conspired against Pekah, killed him, and reigned in his place.

hoshea-2ki-15-30.short: Hoshea son of Elah killed Pekah and became the last king of Israel; in his ninth year the king of Assyria took Samaria and carried Israel away.

paragraphs.text: Hoshea was the son of Elah. He conspired against Pekah the son of Remaliah, killed him, and reigned in his place. He began to reign in Samaria in the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah and reigned nine years. Kings says “he did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD, but not as the kings of Israel that were before him”.

Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against him, and Hoshea became his servant and gave him presents. Then Hoshea sent messengers to So king of Egypt and brought no present to the king of Assyria, as he had done year by year, and the king of Assyria “shut him up, and bound him in prison”. Kings says no more of what became of him.

The king of Assyria came up against Samaria and besieged it three years, and “in the ninth year of Hoshea” he took Samaria and carried Israel away into Assyria. Kings gives the reason at length, beginning: “the children of Israel had sinned against the LORD their God”.

rehoboam-1ki-11-43.short: Solomon's son Rehoboam, born to Naamah the Ammonitess, lost the ten northern tribes at Shechem and reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem.

paragraphs.text: Rehoboam was the son of Solomon and reigned in his place; his mother was Naamah, an Ammonitess. He was forty-one years old when he began to reign. He went to Shechem, where all Israel had come to make him king, and the people asked him to make lighter the heavy yoke his father had put on them.

He forsook the counsel of the old men who had stood before Solomon and answered the people as the young men advised: “my father also chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions”. Israel answered “What portion have we in David?” and went to their tents; they stoned Adoram, who was over the tribute, and Rehoboam fled to Jerusalem. He gathered an army to fight Israel, but Shemaiah the man of God brought the word “Ye shall not go up”, and they went home.

Chronicles adds that he built cities for defence in Judah and Benjamin, and that priests and Levites cast off by Jeroboam came to him from all Israel. He took eighteen wives and sixty concubines and had twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters; he loved Maachah the daughter of Absalom above them all, and made her son Abijah chief among his brothers.

In his fifth year Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem and took away the treasures of the house of the LORD and of the king's house, with the shields of gold Solomon had made; Rehoboam made shields of brass in their place. Chronicles adds that when Shemaiah spoke, the princes of Israel and the king humbled themselves, and the LORD did not destroy them altogether. There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all their days.

Kings says that in his reign “Judah did evil in the sight of the LORD”; Chronicles says of the king, “he did evil, because he prepared not his heart to seek the LORD”. He reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David, and Abijam his son reigned in his place.

abijah-1ki-14-31.short: Rehoboam's son Abijah, called Abijam in Kings, reigned three years in Jerusalem; Chronicles tells of his victory over Jeroboam by Mount Zemaraim.

paragraphs.text: Abijah, whom Kings calls Abijam, was the son of Rehoboam and reigned in his place. Kings names his mother “Maachah, the daughter of Abishalom”; Chronicles once calls her “Michaiah the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah”. Chronicles says Rehoboam loved Maachah above all his wives and made Abijah chief among his brothers, for he meant to make him king.

He began to reign over Judah in the eighteenth year of Jeroboam and reigned three years in Jerusalem. Kings says “he walked in all the sins of his father”, yet for David's sake the LORD gave him “a lamp in Jerusalem”. There was war between Abijam and Jeroboam.

Chronicles adds the battle. Standing on Mount Zemaraim, Abijah reminded Jeroboam and Israel that the LORD gave the kingdom to David and his sons “by a covenant of salt”. Judah, caught between an ambush behind and the army in front, cried to the LORD and won, “because they relied upon the LORD God of their fathers”, and Abijah took Beth-el and other towns. He married fourteen wives and had twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters; he slept with his fathers, was buried in the city of David, and Asa his son reigned in his place.

asa-1ki-15-8.short: Abijah's son Asa reigned forty-one years in Jerusalem, put away idols, removed Maachah from being queen, and in his old age was diseased in his feet.

paragraphs.text: Asa was the son of Abijam and reigned in his place. He began to reign in the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel and reigned forty-one years in Jerusalem. Kings names his mother as Maachah, the daughter of Abishalom, and says “Asa did that which was right in the eyes of the LORD, as did David his father”.

He put away the sodomites and the idols his fathers had made, and he removed Maachah from being queen because she had made an idol in a grove; he burnt her idol by the brook Kidron. The high places were not removed, but “Asa's heart was perfect with the LORD all his days”. Chronicles adds ten quiet years, fenced cities, a victory over Zerah the Ethiopian, and a covenant in his fifteenth year to seek the LORD, after the prophet Azariah son of Oded spoke to him.

There was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days. When Baasha built Ramah so that none could go out or come in to Asa, Asa sent the silver and gold of the house of the LORD and of the king's house to Ben-hadad king of Syria, who broke his league with Baasha. Chronicles adds that Hanani the seer rebuked Asa for relying on the king of Syria, and that Asa put him in prison and oppressed some of the people.

In his old age he was diseased in his feet. Chronicles adds that this was in his thirty-ninth year, that “he sought not to the LORD, but to the physicians”, and that he died in his forty-first year and was laid in his own sepulchre on a bed of spices, with “a very great burning” for him. Kings says he was buried with his fathers in the city of David, and Jehoshaphat his son reigned in his place.

jehoshaphat-1ki-15-24.short: Asa's son Jehoshaphat reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem, walked in his father's ways, made peace with Israel, and fought beside Ahab at Ramoth-gilead.

paragraphs.text: Jehoshaphat was the son of Asa and reigned in his place. He was thirty-five years old when he began to reign, in the fourth year of Ahab king of Israel, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem; his mother was Azubah the daughter of Shilhi. Kings says he walked in all the ways of Asa his father, “doing that which was right in the eyes of the LORD”, though the high places were not taken away.

He made peace with the king of Israel, and Chronicles says he “joined affinity with Ahab”; his son Jehoram married a daughter of Ahab. He went with Ahab against Ramoth-gilead, asked for “a prophet of the LORD besides”, and heard Micaiah. In the battle the captains of the chariots took him for the king of Israel, he cried out, and they turned back from him, but Ahab was killed. Chronicles adds that Jehu the son of Hanani met him on his return: “Shouldest thou help the ungodly, and love them that hate the LORD?”

Chronicles also tells that he sent princes, Levites and priests through the cities of Judah to teach the book of the law of the LORD, and set judges in the land, telling them “ye judge not for man, but for the LORD”. When Moab, Ammon and others came against him, he proclaimed a fast and prayed; Jahaziel told the people “the battle is not yours, but God's”, and the invaders destroyed one another.

He went with Jehoram king of Israel against Moab, and Elisha answered the kings only because “I regard the presence of Jehoshaphat”. His ships, made to go to Ophir for gold, were broken at Ezion-geber; Kings says he would not let Ahaziah king of Israel send his servants with them. Chronicles says he had joined himself with Ahaziah to make the ships, and that the prophet Eliezer said this was why they were broken. He slept with his fathers, was buried in the city of David, and Jehoram his son reigned in his place.

jehoram-1ki-22-50.short: Jehoshaphat's son Jehoram married Ahab's daughter, reigned eight years in Jerusalem, lost Edom, and, Chronicles says, died of a disease of the bowels.

paragraphs.text: Jehoram, also called Joram, was the son of Jehoshaphat and reigned in his place. He was thirty-two years old when he began to reign, and reigned eight years in Jerusalem. Kings says he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as did the house of Ahab, “for the daughter of Ahab was his wife”. Yet the LORD would not destroy Judah, for David his servant's sake.

In his days Edom revolted from Judah and made a king over itself. Jehoram went over to Zair, rose by night and struck the Edomites who surrounded him, but Edom stayed in revolt, and Libnah revolted at the same time.

Chronicles adds more. When he was established, he killed all his brothers, to whom Jehoshaphat had given fenced cities, and some of the princes of Israel. He made high places in the mountains of Judah. A writing came to him from Elijah the prophet, foretelling a plague on his people and his house and a disease of his bowels; then the Philistines and Arabians carried away his goods, his wives and his sons, all but Jehoahaz the youngest.

Kings says he slept with his fathers and was buried with them in the city of David, and Ahaziah his son reigned in his place. Chronicles says that after two years his bowels fell out by reason of his sickness, that he “departed without being desired”, and that he was buried in the city of David, “but not in the sepulchres of the kings”.

ahaziah-2ki-8-24.short: Jehoram's son Ahaziah, whose mother was Athaliah, reigned one year in Jerusalem and was killed in Jehu's revolt.

paragraphs.text: Ahaziah was the son of Jehoram king of Judah and reigned in his place; his mother was Athaliah, “the daughter of Omri king of Israel”. Kings says he was twenty-two years old when he began to reign; Chronicles says forty-two. He reigned one year in Jerusalem. Chronicles adds that the people of Jerusalem made him, the youngest son, king, because raiders had slain all the eldest.

Kings says “he walked in the way of the house of Ahab”; Chronicles adds that “his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly”. He went with Joram the son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth-gilead, and when Joram was wounded, Ahaziah went down to Jezreel to see him.

Jehu met Joram and Ahaziah in the portion of Naboth the Jezreelite and shot Joram, and Ahaziah fled. Kings says he was struck at the going up to Gur by Ibleam, fled to Megiddo and died there, and his servants carried him to Jerusalem and buried him in the city of David. Chronicles says he was found hiding in Samaria, brought to Jehu and slain, and was buried because, they said, “he is the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart”. Jehu also killed forty-two men who said they were “the brethren of Ahaziah”.

athaliah-2ki-8-26.short: Athaliah, King Jehoram's wife and King Ahaziah's mother, destroyed the royal seed and reigned six years, until Jehoiada the priest crowned the hidden Joash.

paragraphs.text: Scripture calls Athaliah “the daughter of Omri”, and says that Jehoram king of Judah married “the daughter of Ahab”. She was the mother of King Ahaziah, and Chronicles says she was “his counsellor to do wickedly”. Scripture does not name her mother.

When she saw that her son Ahaziah was dead, she “arose and destroyed all the seed royal”. But Jehosheba, the daughter of king Joram and sister of Ahaziah, stole away Ahaziah's son Joash with his nurse, and he was hidden in the house of the LORD six years while Athaliah reigned over the land. Chronicles, which calls her Jehoshabeath, adds that she was the wife of Jehoiada the priest.

In the seventh year Jehoiada brought out the king's son and crowned him, and the people clapped their hands and said, “God save the king.” Athaliah heard the noise, came into the house of the LORD, rent her clothes and cried, “Treason, Treason.” Jehoiada would not let her be slain in the house of the LORD, so she was taken out, and slain by the way by which the horses came into the king's house.

joash-2ki-11-2.short: Ahaziah's son Joash, hidden in the temple as a baby, was crowned at seven, repaired the temple, reigned forty years, and was killed by his servants.

paragraphs.text: Joash, also called Jehoash, was the son of Ahaziah king of Judah; his mother was Zibiah of Beer-sheba. When Athaliah destroyed the royal seed, Jehosheba, his father's sister, hid him, and he was kept six years in the house of the LORD. In the seventh year Jehoiada the priest brought him out, crowned him and anointed him; he was seven years old.

He reigned forty years in Jerusalem, and “did that which was right in the sight of the LORD all his days wherein Jehoiada the priest instructed him”. Chronicles adds that Jehoiada took him two wives. In his twenty-third year the priests had still not repaired the breaches of the temple, so Jehoiada set a chest with a hole in its lid beside the altar, and the money was given to the workmen who repaired the house.

Chronicles adds what followed Jehoiada's death. The princes of Judah came to the king, he hearkened to them, and they left the house of the LORD and served groves and idols. When Zechariah the son of Jehoiada spoke against it, they stoned him “at the commandment of the king” in the court of the temple; as he died he said, “The LORD look upon it, and require it.”

When Hazael king of Syria set his face to go up to Jerusalem, Joash sent him the hallowed things and the gold of the temple and the palace, and he went away; Chronicles tells of a small Syrian army that defeated a great host of Judah. His servants conspired and killed him in the house of Millo, and Kings says he was buried with his fathers in the city of David. Chronicles says they killed him on his bed “for the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest”, and buried him in the city of David, but not in the sepulchres of the kings.

amaziah-2ki-12-21.short: Joash's son Amaziah reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem, beat Edom in the valley of salt, was beaten by Jehoash of Israel, and was killed at Lachish.

paragraphs.text: Amaziah was the son of Joash and reigned in his place. He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign and reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem; his mother was Jehoaddan of Jerusalem. Kings says he did that which was right in the sight of the LORD, “yet not like David his father”. When the kingdom was established in his hand he killed the servants who had killed his father, but not their children, as the law of Moses commands.

He killed ten thousand of Edom in the valley of salt and took Selah. Chronicles adds that he had hired a hundred thousand men of Israel and sent them home at the word of a man of God, and that after the victory he brought the gods of the children of Seir home, bowed down to them, and silenced the prophet the LORD sent to rebuke him.

He challenged Jehoash king of Israel, who answered with the parable of the thistle and the cedar. At Beth-shemesh Judah was beaten, and Jehoash took Amaziah, broke down Jerusalem's wall and took the treasures. Amaziah lived fifteen years after the death of Jehoash. When a conspiracy was made against him in Jerusalem he fled to Lachish and was killed there, and they brought him on horses and buried him with his fathers; Chronicles dates the conspiracy from the time he turned away from following the LORD.

uzziah-2ki-14-21.short: Amaziah's son Uzziah, also called Azariah, became king at sixteen, reigned fifty-two years, prospered, and was a leper living apart until he died.

paragraphs.text: Uzziah, whom Kings mostly calls Azariah, was the son of Amaziah; his mother was Jecholiah of Jerusalem. All the people of Judah made him king at sixteen in place of his father, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. He built Elath and restored it to Judah. Kings says “he did that which was right in the sight of the LORD”, though the high places were not removed.

Chronicles adds much more. He sought God in the days of Zechariah, and “as long as he sought the LORD, God made him to prosper”. He broke down the walls of Gath, Jabneh and Ashdod, God helped him against the Arabians and the Mehunims, and he built towers and dug many wells, “for he loved husbandry”. He made engines on the towers to shoot arrows and great stones.

Kings says “the LORD smote the king, so that he was a leper unto the day of his death”, and that he dwelt in a separate house while Jotham his son judged the people. Chronicles gives the cause: when he was strong his heart was lifted up, and he went into the temple to burn incense; Azariah the priest and eighty priests withstood him, and while he was wroth with them the leprosy rose up in his forehead.

He slept with his fathers. Kings says they buried him with his fathers in the city of David; Chronicles says “in the field of the burial which belonged to the kings; for they said, He is a leper”. Isaiah saw the Lord upon a throne “in the year that king Uzziah died”.

jotham-2ki-15-5.short: Uzziah's son Jotham judged the people for his leper father, then reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem and built the higher gate of the temple.

paragraphs.text: Jotham was the son of Uzziah; his mother was Jerusha the daughter of Zadok. While his father was a leper, Jotham “was over the house, judging the people of the land”. He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, in the second year of Pekah king of Israel, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.

Kings says “he did that which was right in the sight of the LORD”, though the high places were not removed, and that he built the higher gate of the house of the LORD. Chronicles adds that he did not enter into the temple of the LORD, that “the people did yet corruptly”, that he built cities in the mountains of Judah and castles and towers in the forests, and that the Ammonites paid him tribute three years. It says “Jotham became mighty, because he prepared his ways before the LORD his God”.

In those days the LORD began to send Rezin king of Syria and Pekah the son of Remaliah against Judah. Jotham slept with his fathers, was buried in the city of David, and Ahaz his son reigned in his place.

ahaz-2ki-15-38.short: Jotham's son Ahaz reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem, made his son pass through the fire, and paid for Assyria's help with the temple's silver and gold.

paragraphs.text: Ahaz was the son of Jotham and reigned in his place. He was twenty years old when he began to reign, in the seventeenth year of Pekah the son of Remaliah, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem; Kings does not name his mother. It says he “did not that which was right in the sight of the LORD his God, like David his father”, but walked in the way of the kings of Israel, “yea, and made his son to pass through the fire”.

Rezin king of Syria and Pekah king of Israel came up to Jerusalem and besieged Ahaz, “but could not overcome him”. The LORD sent Isaiah to meet him at the end of the conduit of the upper pool and tell him not to fear; when Ahaz would not ask a sign, the answer came: “Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.” Chronicles adds heavy defeats, with a hundred and twenty thousand of Judah killed in one day and two hundred thousand taken captive to Samaria.

Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, “I am thy servant and thy son”, with the silver and gold of the temple and the palace, and the Assyrian took Damascus and killed Rezin. When Ahaz went to meet him at Damascus, he sent the pattern of the altar there to Urijah the priest, who built one like it, and he changed the temple's furnishings, turning the covert for the sabbath and the king's entry from the house of the LORD “for the king of Assyria”. Chronicles says the king of Assyria “helped him not”, and adds that Ahaz sacrificed to the gods of Damascus and shut up the doors of the house of the LORD.

He slept with his fathers. Kings says he was buried with his fathers in the city of David; Chronicles says they buried him in Jerusalem, “but they brought him not into the sepulchres of the kings of Israel”. Hezekiah his son reigned in his place.

hezekiah-2ki-16-20.short: Ahaz's son Hezekiah reigned twenty-nine years, removed the high places, trusted the LORD when Sennacherib came, and was granted fifteen more years of life.

paragraphs.text: Hezekiah was the son of Ahaz and reigned in his place. He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem; his mother was Abi the daughter of Zachariah. Kings says he did right “according to all that David his father did”, and “after him was none like him among all the kings of Judah, nor any that were before him”. He removed the high places and broke in pieces the brasen serpent Moses had made, to which Israel had burned incense.

Chronicles adds that in the first month of his first year he opened the doors of the house of the LORD and repaired them, and that he sent to all Israel and Judah to keep the Passover at Jerusalem; since Solomon's time “there was not the like in Jerusalem”. Kings says he rebelled against the king of Assyria and served him not, and that in his sixth year Samaria was taken by Assyria.

In his fourteenth year Sennacherib king of Assyria took the fenced cities of Judah. Hezekiah sent to him at Lachish, “I have offended”, and paid tribute, cutting off the gold from the doors of the temple; still Sennacherib's officers came to Jerusalem and mocked its trust in the LORD. Hezekiah spread the Assyrian's letter before the LORD and prayed, and Isaiah sent him the LORD's answer. That night the angel of the LORD smote the camp of the Assyrians, and Sennacherib went home to Nineveh.

He was “sick unto death”, and Isaiah told him to set his house in order. He turned his face to the wall and prayed and wept, and the LORD added fifteen years to his days, with the sign of the shadow going back ten degrees. When envoys came from Berodach-baladan king of Babylon, he showed them all his treasures, and Isaiah foretold that all would be carried to Babylon. Chronicles adds that his heart was lifted up, but that he humbled himself.

He made a pool and a conduit and brought water into the city. He slept with his fathers, and Manasseh his son reigned in his place. Chronicles says they buried him “in the chiefest of the sepulchres of the sons of David”, and all Judah and Jerusalem did him honour at his death.

manasseh-2ki-20-21.short: Hezekiah's son Manasseh became king at twelve, reigned fifty-five years, and rebuilt the high places; Chronicles adds his captivity in Babylon, his prayer and his return.

paragraphs.text: Manasseh was the son of Hezekiah and reigned in his place. He was twelve years old when he began to reign, and reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem; his mother was Hephzi-bah. Kings says he did evil “after the abominations of the heathen”. He built again the high places his father had destroyed, reared up altars for Baal, built altars for the host of heaven in the two courts of the house of the LORD, made his son pass through the fire, and dealt with familiar spirits and wizards.

The LORD spoke by his servants the prophets that he would wipe Jerusalem “as a man wipeth a dish”. Kings says Manasseh “shed innocent blood very much, till he had filled Jerusalem from one end to another”, and later names his sins as the reason Judah was removed out of the LORD's sight.

Chronicles adds that the captains of the king of Assyria took Manasseh among the thorns, bound him with fetters, and carried him to Babylon. In his affliction he humbled himself and prayed, and God brought him again to Jerusalem: “Then Manasseh knew that the LORD he was God.” Afterward he built a wall outside the city of David, took the strange gods and the idol out of the house of the LORD, and commanded Judah to serve the LORD. Kings has none of this.
He slept with his fathers. Kings says he was buried in the garden of his own house, in the garden of Uzza; Chronicles says they buried him in his own house. Amon his son reigned in his place.

amon-2ki-21-18.short: Manasseh's son Amon reigned two years in Jerusalem, served his father's idols, and was killed by his servants in his own house.

paragraphs.text: Amon was the son of Manasseh and reigned in his place. He was twenty-two years old when he began to reign, and reigned two years in Jerusalem; his mother was Meshullemeth the daughter of Haruz of Jotbah. Kings says he did evil “as his father Manasseh did”, and served the idols his father served. Chronicles adds that he “humbled not himself before the LORD, as Manasseh his father had humbled himself”.

His servants conspired against him and killed him in his own house. The people of the land killed all who had conspired against King Amon and made Josiah his son king in his place. He was buried in his sepulchre in the garden of Uzza.

josiah-1ki-13-2.short: Amon's son Josiah, king at eight, repaired the temple, heard the book of the law, cleansed the land, and died after going out against Pharaoh-nechoh at Megiddo.

paragraphs.text: Josiah was the son of Amon. The people of the land made him king when his father was killed, and he was eight years old when he began to reign; he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem, and his mother was Jedidah the daughter of Adaiah of Boscath. In Jeroboam's day a man of God had cried against the altar at Beth-el: “a child shall be born unto the house of David, Josiah by name”. Kings says he “walked in all the way of David his father, and turned not aside to the right hand or to the left”.

Chronicles says that in his eighth year, “while he was yet young, he began to seek after the God of David his father”, and in his twelfth year began to purge Judah and Jerusalem of the high places and the images. In his eighteenth year, when the temple was being repaired, Hilkiah the high priest found the book of the law; Shaphan read it before the king, and he rent his clothes. Huldah the prophetess sent word that evil would come on the place, but that Josiah would be gathered to his grave in peace.

He gathered the people, read in their ears the book of the covenant, and made a covenant before the LORD. He burned the vessels made for Baal, defiled Topheth, broke down the altar at Beth-el and burned bones upon it, as the man of God had proclaimed, and kept a Passover like none since the days of the judges. Kings says “like unto him was there no king before him, that turned to the LORD with all his heart”.

When Pharaoh-nechoh went up to the river Euphrates, Josiah went against him. Kings says Necho “slew him at Megiddo, when he had seen him”, and his servants carried him dead to Jerusalem and buried him in his own sepulchre. Chronicles adds that Necho sent to warn him, that Josiah disguised himself and was wounded by archers, and that he died after he was brought to Jerusalem; Jeremiah lamented for him.

jehoahaz-2ki-23-30.short: Josiah's son Jehoahaz was made king by the people at twenty-three, reigned three months, and was taken to Egypt by Pharaoh-nechoh, where he died.

paragraphs.text: Jehoahaz was a son of Josiah; his mother was Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah. After Josiah was killed, “the people of the land took Jehoahaz the son of Josiah, and anointed him, and made him king in his father's stead”. He was twenty-three years old and reigned three months in Jerusalem. Kings says he did evil “according to all that his fathers had done”.

Pharaoh-nechoh put him in bands at Riblah in the land of Hamath, laid a tribute on the land, made his brother Eliakim king, and took Jehoahaz away: “he came to Egypt, and died there”. Chronicles says the king of Egypt “put him down at Jerusalem”. Jeremiah speaks of a son of Josiah named Shallum, “which reigned instead of Josiah his father”, who had gone away and would die in the place where he was led captive.

jehoiakim-2ki-23-34.short: Josiah's son Eliakim, renamed Jehoiakim by Pharaoh-nechoh, reigned eleven years, burned Jeremiah's scroll, and rebelled against Babylon.

paragraphs.text: Jehoiakim was born Eliakim, a son of Josiah; his mother was Zebudah the daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah. Pharaoh-nechoh made him king, “turned his name to Jehoiakim”, and took his brother Jehoahaz away to Egypt. He was twenty-five years old and reigned eleven years in Jerusalem, taxing the land to give Pharaoh the silver and gold he demanded. Kings says he did evil “according to all that his fathers had done”.

Jeremiah spoke against him as one “that buildeth his house by unrighteousness”, whose eyes and heart were set on covetousness and on shedding innocent blood. When the prophet Urijah fled to Egypt, Jehoiakim had him brought back and killed with the sword. In his fifth year, as Jeremiah's roll was read to him by the fire, he cut it with a penknife and cast it into the fire until it was consumed.

Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up, and Jehoiakim became his servant three years, then turned and rebelled; bands of Chaldees, Syrians, Moabites and Ammonites came against Judah. Kings says “Jehoiakim slept with his fathers”, and Jehoiachin his son reigned in his place. Chronicles says Nebuchadnezzar “bound him in fetters, to carry him to Babylon”, and Jeremiah had said he would be “buried with the burial of an ass”.

jehoiachin-2ki-24-6.short: Jehoiakim's son Jehoiachin reigned three months, surrendered to Nebuchadnezzar, and spent thirty-seven years a captive in Babylon before Evil-merodach released him.

paragraphs.text: Jehoiachin was the son of Jehoiakim and reigned in his place. Jeremiah speaks of “Coniah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah”, and Chronicles lists Jehoiakim's son as Jeconiah. His mother was Nehushta the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem. Kings says he was eighteen years old and reigned three months; Chronicles says he was eight and reigned three months and ten days. Kings says he did evil “according to all that his father had done”.

When the servants of Nebuchadnezzar besieged Jerusalem, Jehoiachin went out to the king of Babylon with his mother, his servants, his princes and his officers. He was carried away to Babylon with the treasures of the temple and the palace, the mighty men and the craftsmen, and the king of Babylon made Mattaniah, his father's brother, king in his place, and named him Zedekiah. Of Coniah, Jeremiah said: “Write ye this man childless”, for none of his seed would sit upon the throne of David.

In the thirty-seventh year of his captivity Evil-merodach king of Babylon lifted up his head out of prison, spoke kindly to him, and set his throne above the thrones of the kings that were with him in Babylon. He ate bread before the king continually “all the days of his life”. Ezekiel dated a vision by the fifth year of “king Jehoiachin's captivity”.

zedekiah-2ki-24-17.short: Josiah's son Mattaniah, renamed Zedekiah by Nebuchadnezzar, reigned eleven years, rebelled against Babylon, and saw Jerusalem fall before he was blinded and taken captive.

paragraphs.text: Zedekiah was born Mattaniah; Jeremiah calls him “Zedekiah the son of Josiah”, and his mother was Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah, who was also the mother of Jehoahaz. After Jehoiachin was taken, the king of Babylon made Mattaniah king and changed his name to Zedekiah; Kings calls him Jehoiachin's “father's brother”, and Chronicles “his brother”. He was twenty-one years old and reigned eleven years in Jerusalem.

Kings says he did evil “according to all that Jehoiakim had done”; Chronicles adds that he “humbled not himself before Jeremiah the prophet”. He rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar, “who had made him swear by God”. Zedekiah had Jeremiah shut up for his prophecies, yet he also asked him secretly, “Is there any word from the LORD?”, and Jeremiah told him to go out to the king of Babylon's princes and live.

In his ninth year Nebuchadnezzar came against Jerusalem and built forts round it. In his eleventh year, with famine in the city, the city was broken up; the men of war fled by night, and the king went toward the plain. The Chaldeans overtook him in the plains of Jericho and brought him to Riblah, where they killed his sons before his eyes, put out his eyes, bound him with fetters of brass and carried him to Babylon. Jeremiah 52 adds that the king of Babylon “put him in prison till the day of his death”.
